chunks: You claimed that I was jealous of every caliph and revolted against them. If that is so, then the blame is not on you, so the excuse is due to you. "And that is a complaint from which your disgrace is apparent."
ai.seo_question: What is Imam Ali's response to Muawiya's claim of jealousy and revolt against the caliphs?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) turns Muawiya’s accusation of envy and rebellion into a logical proof of Muawiya’s own guilt, asserting that if the charge were true, the blame would rest on the accuser. This rhetorical reversal underscores the Shia view of Ali’s legitimate authority and frames Muawiya’s complaint not as a valid critique, but as a self-incriminating admission of his own political disgrace and deviation from justice.
